leaves.answer: $A' = B$: A and B are the transpose of each other.
leaves.why: Writing the rows of A as columns gives $\begin{bmatrix} a_1 & b_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 \end{bmatrix} = B$.

leaves.answer: $B' = A$: A and B are the transpose of each other.
leaves.why: Writing the rows of B as columns gives A.

leaves.answer: $C' = D$: C and D are the transpose of each other.
leaves.why: The rows $(-3, 1, -1)$ and $(4, 2, 7)$ of C are the columns of D.

leaves.answer: $D' = C$: C and D are the transpose of each other.
leaves.why: The columns of D are the rows of C.
D is a $2 \times 3$ matrix; only a square matrix can be symmetric.
The diagonal is 0 and $a_{12} = 4 = -a_{21}$, so $A' = -A$.
The diagonal is 0 and $a_{12} = -5 = -a_{21}$, so $B' = -B$.
$a_{12} = a_{21} = 7$, so $C' = C$; skew-symmetry needs $a_{21} = -a_{12}$.
A and B have the same order, $2 \times 3$.
B is $2 \times 3$ and D is $2 \times 2$: matrices of different orders cannot be added.
$3A$ is $2 \times 3$ and $2C$ is $2 \times 2$: different orders.
C and D are both $2 \times 2$. (The printed key lists this one as (ii).)
Each pair of corresponding entries adds up to 0.
Every entry of F is the negative of the entry of E in the same place.

leaves.answer: A is $2 \times 1$: $AB$ ($2 \times 2$) and $AD$ ($2 \times 3$) are defined, and $CA$ ($2 \times 1$) is defined with A second. Conformable products: $AB, BA, CA, BC, AD$.
leaves.why: A product $XY$ is defined when the number of columns of X equals the number of rows of Y.

leaves.answer: B is $1 \times 2$: $BA$ ($1 \times 1$) and $BC$ ($1 \times 2$) are defined, and $AB$ is defined with B second. Conformable products: $AB, BA, CA, BC, AD$.
leaves.why: B has 2 columns, which match the 2 rows of A and of C.

leaves.answer: C is $2 \times 2$: $CA$ ($2 \times 1$) is defined, and $BC$ ($1 \times 2$) is defined with C second. Conformable products: $AB, BA, CA, BC, AD$.
leaves.why: C has 2 rows and 2 columns, matching A (2 rows) and B (2 columns).

leaves.answer: D is $1 \times 3$: only $AD$ ($2 \times 3$) is defined, with D second. Conformable products: $AB, BA, CA, BC, AD$.
leaves.why: D has 3 columns and none of A, B, C has 3 rows, so D cannot come first.
$|A| = 5 \cdot 1 - 3 \cdot 2 = -1 \neq 0$.
$|C| = 3a \cdot b - (-2b)(2a) = 3ab + 4ab = 7ab \neq 0$.

Every power of y is a whole number (0, 1, 2, 3) and the coefficients are real numbers.
$\dfrac{5}{x^2}$ and $\dfrac{3}{4x + 1}$ have the variable in a denominator (negative power of x).
It contains $\sqrt{x} = x^{1/2}$ (a power that is not a whole number) and a denominator with x.

leaves.answer: Not in its lowest terms: it equals $5(y + 1)$.
leaves.why: $\dfrac{5y^2 - 5}{y - 1} = \dfrac{5(y - 1)(y + 1)}{y - 1}$ has the common factor $y - 1$. (The printed key says the opposite: it lists (i) and (iii) as lowest terms.)
$\dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x - 2} = \dfrac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{x - 2}$: the numerator and denominator have no common factor. (The printed key says it is not.)

leaves.answer: Not in its lowest terms: it equals $\dfrac{1}{x - y}$.
leaves.why: $\dfrac{x + y}{x^2 - y^2} = \dfrac{x + y}{(x - y)(x + y)}$ has the common factor $x + y$.
The book's test: a number is a surd when it is irrational, a root, and a root of a rational number. $\sqrt[3]{81} = 3\sqrt[3]{3}$ is an irrational cube root of a rational number.
It is the square root of $1 + \sqrt{5}$, which is irrational: it is not a root of a rational number. (The printed key lists (i), (ii).)
$\sqrt{\sqrt{5}} = \sqrt[4]{5}$, an irrational fourth root of the rational number 5.
$\sqrt[4]{32} = 2\sqrt[4]{2}$ is an irrational root of a rational number.
$\pi$ is irrational but it is not a root of a rational number.
It is the square root of $1 + \pi^2$, which is irrational, not rational.

steps.en: Write $y = 2x + 6$ and make a table: $x = -3 \Rightarrow y = 0$; $x = -1 \Rightarrow y = 4$; $x = 0 \Rightarrow y = 6$.
Plot $(-3, 0)$, $(-1, 4)$, $(0, 6)$ and join them with a ruler: the line has slope 2.
Table for $y = 1 - x$: $x = -1 \Rightarrow y = 2$; $x = 0 \Rightarrow y = 1$; $x = 1 \Rightarrow y = 0$; $x = 2 \Rightarrow y = -1$.
Plot the points and join them: the line falls from left to right.

leaves.answer: A horizontal line through $(0, 2)$, parallel to the x-axis.

steps.en: Every point of the line has $y = 2$ whatever x is: $(-2, 2)$, $(0, 2)$, $(3, 2)$.
Plot these points and draw the line through them.

leaves.answer: A straight line through the origin with slope 1: $(-2, -2)$, $(0, 0)$, $(3, 3)$.

steps.en: Table for $y = x$: $x = -2 \Rightarrow y = -2$; $x = 0 \Rightarrow y = 0$; $x = 3 \Rightarrow y = 3$.
Plot the points and join them: the line bisects the angle between the positive axes.

The sum of any two sides is greater than the third: $2 + 2 > 2$.
$5 + 2 = 7$ is less than 8, so the two shorter sides cannot reach across the longest.
$1\frac{1}{2} + 3\frac{1}{2} = 5$, which is not greater than 5: the three lengths would lie on a straight line.
$2\frac{1}{2} + 3\frac{1}{2} = 6 > 4\frac{1}{2}$, and the other two sums are larger still.

leaves.answer: $\triangle PBC$ and $\triangle QBC$ are equal in area.
leaves.why: They stand on the same base BC and lie between the same parallels PQ and BC.

leaves.answer: $\triangle BRP$ and $\triangle CRQ$ are equal in area.
leaves.why: $\triangle BRP = \triangle PBC - \triangle RBC$ and $\triangle CRQ = \triangle QBC - \triangle RBC$; the two triangles on the right are equal by (i).

leaves.answer: $\triangle PQB$ and $\triangle PQC$ are equal in area.
leaves.why: They stand on the same base PQ and lie between the same parallels PQ and BC.

leaves.answer: $\triangle ABQ$ and $\triangle ACP$ are equal in area.
leaves.why: $\triangle ABQ = \triangle APQ + \triangle PQB$ and $\triangle ACP = \triangle APQ + \triangle PQC$; $\triangle PQB = \triangle PQC$ by (iii).

leaves.answer: The three angle bisectors meet at one point, the incentre; the inradius is about 1.08 cm.

steps.en: Construct the triangle with AB = 4.5 cm, BC = 3.1 cm, CA = 5.2 cm (arcs from the ends of one side).
Bisect each of the three angles with compass arcs and a ruler.
The three bisectors pass through one point I, the incentre. Check: the perpendicular distance from I to each side is the same, about 1.08 cm.

leaves.answer: The three angle bisectors meet at one point, the incentre (also the centroid of an equilateral triangle); the inradius is about 3.46 for side 12.

steps.en: Construct the equilateral triangle of side 12 (all three arcs of radius 12).
Bisect the three angles (each 60° becomes 30°): the bisectors meet at the incentre, and the distance from it to each side is $12/(2\sqrt{3}) \approx 3.46$.

leaves.answer: The three angle bisectors meet at one point, the incentre; the triangle has $\angle B = 60^\circ$, $BC \approx 4.74$ cm, $AB \approx 6.47$ cm, and the inradius is about 1.56 cm.

steps.en: Draw CA = 5.8 cm, make $\angle A = 45^\circ$ and $\angle C = 75^\circ$; the rays meet at B.
Bisect the three angles: the bisectors meet at the incentre, equally far (about 1.56 cm) from the three sides.

leaves.answer: The three altitudes meet at one point, the orthocentre. The triangle (6, 4.5, 5.5 cm) is acute, so the orthocentre lies inside it.

steps.en: Construct the triangle with PQ = 6 cm, QR = 4.5 cm, PR = 5.5 cm.
From each vertex draw the perpendicular to the opposite side; the three lines meet at the orthocentre H, inside the triangle because $6^2 < 4.5^2 + 5.5^2$ (all angles acute).

leaves.answer: The three altitudes meet at one point, the orthocentre. The triangle has $PR \approx 6.31$ cm and is obtuse at Q ($\approx 97.2^\circ$), so the orthocentre lies outside it.

steps.en: Draw QR = 3.9 cm, make $\angle R = 45^\circ$ and cut off PQ = 4.5 cm with an arc from Q on the ray from R: $\sin P = 3.9 \sin 45^\circ / 4.5$ gives $P \approx 37.8^\circ$, so $Q \approx 97.2^\circ$.
Draw the altitudes (extend the sides where needed); they meet outside the triangle.

leaves.answer: The three altitudes meet at one point, the orthocentre. The third angle is $R = 45^\circ$, so the triangle is acute and the orthocentre lies inside.

steps.en: Draw PQ = 6 cm, make $\angle P = 70^\circ$ and $\angle Q = 65^\circ$; the rays meet at R ($\angle R = 45^\circ$).
Draw the altitudes from P, Q and R: they meet at the orthocentre H inside the triangle.

leaves.answer: The three perpendicular bisectors meet at one point, the circumcentre. The triangle (7, 6.5, 5.8 cm) is acute, so the circumcentre lies inside; the circumradius is about 3.75 cm.

steps.en: Construct the triangle with UV = 7 cm, VW = 6.5 cm, WU = 5.8 cm.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of each side (arcs of equal radius from both ends); they meet at O, equally far from U, V and W.

leaves.answer: The three perpendicular bisectors meet at one point, the circumcentre. The triangle is obtuse at W, so the circumcentre lies outside it; $UV \approx 12.63$ cm and the circumradius is about 7.29 cm.

steps.en: Draw VW = 10 cm, make $\angle W = 120^\circ$ and cut off WU = 4.2 cm; then $UV = \sqrt{10^2 + 4.2^2 - 2(10)(4.2)\cos 120^\circ} \approx 12.63$ cm.
Draw the three perpendicular bisectors; they meet at O outside the triangle, equally far (about 7.29 cm) from U, V and W.

leaves.answer: The three perpendicular bisectors meet at one point, the circumcentre (the centre of an equilateral triangle); the circumradius is about 0.46 m.

steps.en: Construct the equilateral triangle of side 0.8 m.
The perpendicular bisectors meet at the centre O; its distance to each vertex is $0.8/\sqrt{3} \approx 0.46$ m.

leaves.answer: The three medians meet at one point, the centroid, which divides each median 2 : 1 from the vertex. The triangle has $\angle Z = 45^\circ$, $XY \approx 3.00$ cm, $XZ \approx 3.68$ cm.

steps.en: Draw YZ = 4.1 cm, make $\angle Y = 60^\circ$ and $\angle Z = 45^\circ$ (since $\angle X = 75^\circ$); the rays meet at X.
Bisect each side to find its midpoint and join it to the opposite vertex: the three medians meet at the centroid G, with $XG : G(\text{midpoint}) = 2 : 1$.

leaves.answer: The three medians meet at one point, the centroid, which divides each median 2 : 1 from the vertex. The triangle has $\angle Z = 60^\circ$, $YZ \approx 5.87$ cm, $XY \approx 5.27$ cm.

steps.en: Draw ZX = 4.3 cm, make $\angle X = 75^\circ$ and $\angle Z = 60^\circ$; the rays meet at Y ($\angle Y = 45^\circ$).
Draw the three medians: they meet at the centroid G, 2 : 1 from each vertex.

leaves.answer: The three medians meet at one point, the centroid, which divides each median 2 : 1 from the vertex.

steps.en: Construct the triangle with XY = 4.5 cm, YZ = 3.4 cm, ZX = 5.6 cm ($4.5 + 3.4 > 5.6$, so it exists).
Join each vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side: the medians meet at the centroid G, and each is cut 2 : 1 at G.
